O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The frame-length route is already closed at kafka/protocol/parser.py:115. The remaining SCRAM site kafka/sasl/scram.py:102 is the advisory's own fix, not an out-of-scope module, and both SASL v0 (SaslBytesRequest) and v1 (SaslAuthenticateRequest) reach it through the single call at kafka/net/connection.py:460.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver led by the 'frame length' summary sees that parser.py already validates frame size and might conclude it is fixed. The SCRAM iteration count is a different kind of server-controlled size (CPU, not memory), and the solver could argue it is 'authentication, not framing'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate SCRAM exchanges with normal iteration counts (Kafka default 4096, up to 16384) must still authenticate, so a fix that caps too low or rejects valid counts breaks SASL/SCRAM login. User-side credential creation with caller-chosen iterations (UserScramCredentialUpsertion) is a separate PBKDF2 use that must not be capped.

O6_input_shapes: non-integer iteration string (int() ValueError, re-raised as ValueError)
negative frame length (already handled at pinned, kafka/protocol/parser.py:144)
frame length above receive_message_max_bytes (already handled at pinned)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Array element count decoded from the wire with no bound before allocating/iterating
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Length-prefixed decoders in the same codec layer read sizes from broker data. A maintainer adding a frame cap could plausibly forget the per-field counts. Inside a bounded frame, though, this mostly costs time rather than memory (low lever per lessons: resource exhaustion).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Tagged-field count/size taken from the wire unbounded
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same codec family as the frame length; a planted unbounded read would look natural. It is a WHERE-type sibling, though, and a resource-exhaustion one.

O9_family: CWE-789 / CWE-400 uncontrolled resource consumption from server-supplied size fields (frame length -> memory; SCRAM iteration count -> CPU)
